title: Linear / Traditional TV Media Planning Checklist for QSR / Restaurants Brands
metaDescription: A practical linear TV media planning checklist tailored for QSR / Restaurants brands — strategy, inventory, optimization, and measurement.
intro: This checklist helps QSR / Restaurants teams plan, buy, and measure linear TV campaigns with fewer missed details. Use it as a pre-launch QA list and as a weekly in-flight operating rhythm.

items.title: Define QSR / Restaurants audience segments and viewing contexts
items.description: Start with 2–4 core segments tied to QSR / Restaurants. For linear TV, map when those audiences are most likely to watch (dayparts, live events, seasonality) so you can align reach with real viewing habits instead of generic demos.

items.title: Set a reach and frequency goal (and the tradeoff)
items.description: Linear TV excels at broad reach but can overserve if frequency is unmanaged. Define your ideal weekly frequency range for QSR / Restaurants and decide where you will cap, rotate, or shift budget to maintain efficient incremental reach.

items.title: Choose a KPI hierarchy (awareness → response)
items.description: Pick leading indicators (reach, GRPs, brand lift proxies) and lagging indicators (site traffic, searches, store visits) that fit QSR / Restaurants. Make sure the KPI set is feasible with your measurement stack before you commit.

items.title: Select programming environments that fit the buying thesis
items.description: For QSR / Restaurants, list 5–10 program genres, networks, or tentpole events that match your audience and brand safety needs. Prioritize placements where linear TV delivery is reliable and context aligns with your creative message.

items.title: Document competitive spend windows and counter-programming
items.description: Note when competitors in QSR / Restaurants typically burst (product launches, seasonal peaks). Use linear TV’s predictability to defend key windows or find efficient counter-programming where CPMs are lower but attention is high.

items.title: Plan creative rotation to avoid wear-out
items.description: Build a rotation plan (at least 3–5 creative variants) and tie swaps to frequency or week number. Linear TV wear-out is common in narrow demos; having a plan reduces performance drop-off in QSR / Restaurants flights.

items.title: Confirm geo strategy (national vs. local split)
items.description: If your QSR / Restaurants outcomes are local (stores, regional demand), define which markets get incremental weight and why. For national buys, document any exclusions and ensure affiliates or local inventory isn’t double-counted.

items.title: Align budget to flighting (always-on vs. pulses)
items.description: Decide whether your linear TV plan for QSR / Restaurants should be always-on for baseline reach or pulsed around key moments. Tie flighting to production timelines so creative arrives before impressions do.

items.title: Validate category compliance and claims
items.description: Certain QSR / Restaurants categories have strict claim rules. Confirm legal/compliance review for linear TV scripts (superimposed text, disclosures, offer terms) early to prevent missed air dates.

items.title: Define success criteria for optimization decisions
items.description: Write down what triggers a change: e.g., underdelivery vs. GRP goal, cost-per-reach point thresholds, or brand lift deltas. Linear TV optimization cycles are slower, so decision rules matter for QSR / Restaurants.

items.title: Lock down the target demo and any audience overlays
items.description: List your primary demo and any overlays relevant to QSR / Restaurants (income, life stage, household). Clarify whether the buy is strictly demo-based or if you will use data-driven linear where available.

items.title: Build a network/program short list with rationale
items.description: Create a short list of networks and program types that index well for QSR / Restaurants. Add a one-line rationale for each so stakeholders understand why a placement is in (or out).

items.title: Estimate reach curves using prior campaigns or benchmarks
items.description: Use last year’s QSR / Restaurants linear TV performance, if available, to estimate reach at different spend levels. If you don’t have history, document the benchmark source and assumptions so you can recalibrate mid-flight.

items.title: Confirm daypart strategy and delivery expectations
items.description: Dayparts drive both cost and audience composition. Define which dayparts are mandatory vs. flexible for QSR / Restaurants, and note where you’ll accept makegoods if delivery shifts.

items.title: Plan for makegoods and preemptions
items.description: Linear TV often requires makegoods when programs are preempted (sports overruns, breaking news). Define acceptable makegood rules up front so the QSR / Restaurants plan doesn’t drift from the original strategy.

items.title: Coordinate with CTV/streaming plans to avoid duplicated reach
items.description: If you also run CTV, define how linear TV contributes incremental reach for QSR / Restaurants. Align audiences and reporting so you can understand overlap and avoid paying twice for the same households.

items.title: Finalize creative specs and trafficking checklist
items.description: Confirm spot lengths, formats, and closed-captioning requirements. Linear TV trafficking errors can delay air dates; a single standardized checklist reduces rework for QSR / Restaurants campaigns.

items.title: Confirm measurement tags and attribution plan
items.description: Linear TV attribution often uses matched market tests, lift studies, or modeled attribution. Document how you will capture response for QSR / Restaurants (vanity URLs, call tracking, time-series lift) before launch.

items.title: Set up a weekly reporting cadence
items.description: Create a repeatable weekly dashboard: delivery vs. plan, GRPs, reach estimates, and outcome proxies. Linear TV planning benefits from consistency so you can compare QSR / Restaurants flights apples-to-apples.

items.title: Define contingency inventory options
items.description: Have 2–3 backup networks or dayparts in case inventory tightens. For QSR / Restaurants, contingency options keep pacing on track without sacrificing brand safety or audience fit.

items.title: Monitor pacing vs. weekly GRP targets
items.description: Check pacing weekly and compare planned vs. delivered GRPs. If QSR / Restaurants delivery is behind, adjust network mix or dayparts early rather than waiting until the end of the flight.

items.title: Review frequency distribution to reduce overserve
items.description: Ask for frequency distributions (not just averages). If a subset of the QSR / Restaurants demo is seeing too many ads, consider creative rotation, schedule shifts, or reallocating to incremental reach tactics.

items.title: Analyze program-level performance proxies
items.description: Use available signals—site traffic spikes, branded search lift, or call volume—by airing window. For QSR / Restaurants, this helps you identify which environments are delivering attention even if direct attribution is limited.

items.title: Adjust creative based on learnings (message-market fit)
items.description: If a specific QSR / Restaurants segment responds better to a certain message (price vs. quality vs. availability), update rotation rules and ensure the right creative runs in the right programs and markets.

items.title: Track competitive activity and react quickly
items.description: If competitors in QSR / Restaurants increase share of voice during your flight, consider short bursts in high-attention programming or rebalancing to protect reach targets.

items.title: Validate makegoods and post logs weekly
items.description: Reconcile airing logs against invoices. For QSR / Restaurants campaigns, missed spots can materially impact reach; catching issues early avoids end-of-flight surprises.

items.title: Coordinate cross-channel creative sequencing
items.description: If digital retargeting follows linear TV exposure, ensure timing and messaging are aligned. For QSR / Restaurants, sequencing can turn awareness into measurable response when TV alone is hard to attribute.

items.title: Update stakeholders with decisions, not just metrics
items.description: Weekly updates should include what changed and why (network swaps, market weights, creative rotation). This keeps QSR / Restaurants leadership aligned and reduces second-guessing.

items.title: Document learnings for the next planning cycle
items.description: Capture which networks, dayparts, and markets were most efficient for QSR / Restaurants. Linear TV planning improves over time when learnings are written down and reused.

items.title: Prepare a post-campaign analysis framework early
items.description: Define how you’ll evaluate the flight: delivery, reach, brand lift, and outcome proxies. For QSR / Restaurants, early planning ensures you can secure the data needed for a credible readout.

items.title: Run a lift analysis windowed to airings
items.description: Compare response (traffic, searches, conversions) in windows around linear TV airings. For QSR / Restaurants, windowed analysis can reveal impact patterns even without perfect user-level attribution.

items.title: Quantify incremental reach vs. streaming/video plans
items.description: Estimate overlap and incremental households reached by linear TV. Knowing incremental reach helps justify the linear portion of the QSR / Restaurants mix in future budget conversations.

items.title: Audit creative and offer compliance in final deliverables
items.description: Ensure the final report includes proof of compliance (disclosures, offer terms) where relevant. This is especially important in regulated QSR / Restaurants categories.

items.title: Create a reusable media plan template for next quarter
items.description: Turn your flight plan into a template: goals, assumptions, network mix, market weights, and reporting cadence. For QSR / Restaurants, this reduces time-to-plan in the next cycle.

items.title: Identify 2–3 test ideas for the next flight
items.description: Based on results, propose tests like new networks, different dayparts, or creative messaging. Linear TV improvements for QSR / Restaurants often come from disciplined experimentation.

items.title: Package insights for stakeholders and partners
items.description: Write a one-page summary: what worked, what didn’t, and what you’ll do next. For QSR / Restaurants, concise insights help secure support for future linear TV investment.

items.title: Map learnings to complementary channels
items.description: If linear TV drove awareness but not response, outline how paid social, search, or CTV can capture demand. For QSR / Restaurants, cross-channel planning makes TV impact more measurable.

items.title: Update your measurement stack for the next run
items.description: If attribution was a pain point, list the exact gaps (spot-level logs, geo-level outcomes, lift study access). Closing those gaps increases confidence in linear TV decisions for QSR / Restaurants.

items.title: Confirm next quarter’s budget and buying timelines
items.description: Linear TV requires lead times. For QSR / Restaurants, confirm upfront vs. scatter approach, and lock key milestones (RFP, creative delivery, trafficking) to avoid rushed decisions.

items.title: Add a “do this again / don’t do this again” checklist item
items.description: The final step is operational: capture 3 repeatable wins and 3 avoidable mistakes. This makes the next QSR / Restaurants linear TV plan better with less effort.

proTips: For QSR / Restaurants, reserve time in the timeline for clearance/standards review so the flight doesn't slip.
Ask for post logs in a consistent format every week so reporting doesn't become manual.
Treat makegoods like inventory, not freebies—ensure they still match your strategy.
Pair TV bursts with search/paid social coverage to capture the demand TV creates.
Write down assumptions (reach curves, CPMs, daypart mix) so you can learn and iterate next cycle.
